english: J.S: Did you used to watch them making Bluebread?
Yes.
Could you tell me about that?
Yeah, yeah. Blue bread too was made of white corn.
Because its white corn powder, for a long time
(That's how one cooks (corn) bluebread dumplings)
For the bluebread dumplings, the hashings get roasted in the oven.
With the water put near the fire, for the lye --- take the ash from near the fire --- and sifting,
with it in the water, stir it over the head, and set it up near the fire, then
if you do it that way, while boiling the water, put it in the water, make it a decent bit clearer, clearer, stir it a little bit, stir it, until its just ready,
and when its ready, take it out of the water, washing it, washing it until its done; in water.
bring along the corn that was scraped off, put it in the mortar, and grinding, grinding, they would pulverize it,
and using a sifter basket, sifting sifting with it, and when they finished they would do it again
They dipped it repeatedly into the thing standing by the fire once it was boiling, dipping it in there and stirring it with the water into a batter,
knead it, knead it, now its ready,
Take it from the fire, out of the water completely, and eat it.
(Moreover, wasn't it enjoyed with fat drippings?)
Yes, it's good. If eaten with pork cracklings, its good.
